transient expression from Sf9 insect cell cultures can be used to produce high levels of recombinant protein in the absence of virus.

the development of a method for virus-free, transient gene expression from insect cells, which can be applied to the rapid production of proteins for research and development, or for use in preclinical studies.
the development of a method for the production of recombinants from suspension-adaptation Sf9 cells using transient transfection.
the development of a method for virus-free production of recombinants in Sf9 insect cell cultures.

the virus-free transient gene transfection system described here can be used for the production of proteins from Sf 9 insect cells at a scale of 1-300 mL.

transient expression of recombinant protein is more efficient than the BEVS in Sf9 insect cell cultures.

transient transfection of insect cells is a viable alternative to BEVS for protein production, especially for proteins that are difficult to produce in BEVS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transient expression from Sf9 suspension cells is a viable method for rapid recombinant protein production.

transient transfection is a viable option for protein production from Sf9 insect cell lines, and that the transient transfection system is more efficient than the baculoviral expression system in terms of the time required to produce recombinant proteins.
